items.title: Dipke breaks silence from Hingoli on the morning re-detention: 'hoisting the flag is not a crime'
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke gave a press interaction to reporters in Hingoli, Maharashtra on Tuesday morning, his first on-camera statement since Delhi Police re-detained co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (and Ajinkya Shinde) for climbing the Jantar Mantar gate with the tricolour. Dipke asked 'since when did hoisting the national flag become a crime', called anyone who treats flag-hoisting as a violation a 'deshdrohi' (traitor), described the action as the biggest example of a dictatorial mentality, declared Jantar Mantar belongs to all 140 crore Indians, and vowed they will continue to hoist the flag there until CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns - closing with a prediction of escalation: 'Now, there will be movements across the entire country, and there will be movements throughout Delhi.' Corroborated by The Hindu (PTI video), IANS and Deccan Chronicle.
